bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Q1FY27 metrics slide shows "INR 255.6 Cr NET CASH & EQUIV." alongside "Net Debt – INR 615.4 Cr" on the same tile; the deck does not reconcile the two labels.
- Balance sheet at Jun-26 versus Mar-26: non-current borrowings INR 533.5 Cr (from INR 682.6 Cr) and current borrowings INR 337.5 Cr (from INR 238.7 Cr); total assets INR 3,659.1 Cr with goodwill of INR 1,591.5 Cr and other intangible assets of INR 756.3 Cr.
- Sojern deferred deal consideration is a recurring charge "to be incurred for 3 years ending Q3FY29", and is the sole reconciling item between reported and adjusted EBITDA/PAT.
- Free cash flow series of 47.5 / 148.1 / 113.4 / 230.0 / 135.2 (INR Cr) for FY2023 through Q1FY2027, with a stated 49.3% CAGR.
- Promoter group (Bhanu Chopra & Family) holds 48.78% and "has increased holding up from 48.16% as of Sept. 30, 2025"; no dividend or buyback policy is discussed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Proprietary data moat built over 20 years of compounding data-collection investment across hotels, airlines, OTAs, car rentals and cruises, processing billions of price points daily across 160+ countries; sources actively block automated collection via website blockers, CAPTCHAs, rate limiting and legal restrictions, so replication requires a proprietary acquisition engine — 'no competitor comes close at this scale'.
- AI models (Rev-AI, Demand-AI, Navigator AI) trained on this dataset improve as the data grows, and improved outcomes earn more under a performance-based revenue model — a compounding loop rather than a commoditising one.
- Certified connectivity: distribution connections are non-standardised and fragmented, channels impose rigorous certification on distribution partners, and trust is earned through multi-year track records of zero execution error, which new entrants cannot short-circuit.
- Full-funnel platform breadth after Sojern — combining consented traveler intent data with RateGain's pricing and distribution infrastructure into an integrated RevMax platform described as difficult for competitors to replicate.
- Scale of the travel-intent intelligence ecosystem: Sojern's travel intent data combined with Adara's data assets and RateGain's commercial intelligence.
- Diversified geographic revenue base across North America (58.8%), Europe (24.9%) and Asia Pacific (14.6%), with exports at 81.02% of turnover and markets served in 160 countries.
- Demonstrated M&A track record — DHISCO (2018), BCV (2019), MyHotelShop (2021), Adara (2023) and Sojern (2025) — each broadening capabilities, product portfolio and the global customer base.
- RateGain Labs, a dedicated in-house incubator for data-driven travel solutions, plus interoperability across a diversified product suite enabling bundling and cross-sell.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data security and customer privacy / cyber-attacks — Identified in the BRSR material responsible business conduct table as a Risk with negative financial implication. Cyber-attacks are described as a critical risk to operations and to the security and trust of customers, with potential to disrupt business continuity, compromise sensitive data and undermine the integrity of digital systems — and beyond the operational impact, to severely damage reputation and erode customer confidence. Mitigation cited: developing applications with near-zero vulnerabilities, robust control mechanisms to detect, manage and mitigate breaches, and an ongoing SOC 2 certification exercise for external assurance.
- Anti-competitive behaviour and conduct in client engagements — Identified in the BRSR material issues table as a Risk with negative financial implication. The Company notes that any lapse in its market-facing efforts to onboard marquee clients could lead to significant reputational risk, and relies on internal controls, policies and procedures designed to prevent inadvertent anti-competitive behaviour.
- AI-led disintermediation of travel discovery and booking — The MD&A describes CY 2026 as a structural inflection where AI begins to mediate decisions before brands ever enter the picture: Google's dominance of travel search is eroding, search is becoming recommendation-led, and influence over travel demand is shifting toward a broader set of digital gatekeepers. AI platforms are extending integrations beyond OTAs to direct hotel connections, global distribution systems and loyalty-rich ecosystems, reshaping who captures margin across the value chain — a shift that can move the customer interface away from incumbent channels RateGain serves.
- Geopolitical instability, border policy and tariffs suppressing travel demand — Shifting global alliances and unpredictable border policies are described as making international travel more difficult than at any point in recent memory, while tariffs and sustained inflation squeeze middle-market travelers. Inbound travel to the U.S. has been on a broadly downward trend since February 2025 following the announcement of new policies and tariffs, with international arrivals estimated down 6% year-on-year in 2025 — material given North America remains the Company's largest market.
- K-shaped travel economy and softening consumer confidence — Tariffs and inflation are creating a distinctly 'K-shaped' travel economy in which luxury segments thrive while budget-conscious travelers trade down to cheaper flights, shorter trips and less expensive destinations. Near-term headwinds flagged include policy uncertainty, a softening job market and the lingering effects of tariffs, creating a mixed backdrop for hotels where visitor volumes remain relatively stable but broader economic signals are inconsistent.
- Sojern integration and execution risk — The Chairman describes a year of integration as involving unifying technology platforms, harmonizing teams across continents, rationalizing overlapping products and asking people to work differently — all while growing. The Adara brand has been retired and all marketing technology now goes to market under Sojern, so the value of the most consequential acquisition since the IPO depends on continued execution of platform, team and commercial consolidation.
- Acquisition-related leverage — The Sojern acquisition was debt-funded; the Company reports having repaid USD 31.5 million of acquisition-related debt — over 25% of the original loan — and states it remains on track to be debt-free by FY 2027-28. Until then the balance sheet carries acquisition debt that was not present before the transaction.
- Geographic concentration and regional demand swings — North America remains the Company's largest market while APAC is the fastest-growing region (team strength grown from 15 to 85 people during FY 2025-26) and Europe is the next investment priority following the Sojern footprint. Management explicitly notes the Middle East faced genuine headwinds during the year, so results remain exposed to region-specific demand shocks.
- Revenue increasingly tied to customer outcomes — Over 70% of revenue is now tied to measurable outcomes for customers under performance-linked pricing — described as 'the commercial model of an AI company, not a software company'. This aligns RateGain with customer success but makes revenue more sensitive to customers' own commercial performance than a pure subscription model would be.

business.body: RateGain provides SaaS solutions to the global travel and hospitality industry across three lines: Data-as-a-Service (rate and demand intelligence), Distribution (sharing availability, rates, inventory and content with OTAs) and MarTech (an end-to-end AI-powered digital marketing suite). Its customers include hotels and global hotel chains, online travel agencies, airlines, car rental providers, cruise operators, travel management companies, destinations and Fortune-listed enterprises. Following the 2025 acquisition of Sojern, the company positions itself as an integrated, full-funnel revenue-maximization (RevMax) platform spanning guest acquisition, engagement and wallet expansion.

outlook.body:
- Unify the entire customer lifecycle and revenue journey into one intelligent, connected 'Rev OS' — an operating system for travel lifecycle revenue spanning dreaming, planning, discovery, booking, experience and retention — by unifying demand, pricing and distribution into a single system with end-to-end control across demand signals (MarTech), pricing intelligence and distribution execution.
- Adopt an AI-first approach in which AI is the intelligence layer rather than a separate capability: embed AI across every product in the Revenue OS so each solution learns from shared traveler intent, commercial signals and guest interactions, creating an intelligence moat that is difficult to replicate.
- Build the three AI vectors — traveler intent, pricing and distribution — supported by the right data at scale, the right safeguards (enterprise-grade security, privacy and governance, responsible AI deployment) and real problems solved (faster automated decisions, greater productivity, better guest experiences).
- Complete the Sojern integration and value unlock: unify Adara into Sojern under a single brand, consolidate technology onto one platform, consolidate Adara and Sojern data partnerships for cost efficiency and a stronger data moat, and migrate customers to the unified platform.
- Commercialize AI agents — shifting from tools that assist to agents that do the work, now generating measurable revenue for customers.
- Launch and scale a unified go-to-market: integrated solutions and aligned GTM teams to deliver a seamless customer experience, with Boston Consulting Group consulted to unify that GTM motion.
- Maximize value across the customer lifecycle through three plays — guest acquisition (converting travel intent into direct traffic, direct bookings and repeat purchase), guest engagement (satisfaction and loyalty through personalized engagement) and guest wallet expansion (upsell and cross-sell).
- Cross-sell the conversational revenue platform alongside UNO ('efforts are underway to cross-sell it alongside UNO').
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: RateGain is an asset-light SaaS business whose expansion is inorganic and go-to-market led rather than plant-based; the annual report discloses no manufacturing capacity or rupee capex quantum. The defining expansion of FY 2025-26 was the acquisition of Sojern Inc. through wholly owned subsidiary RateGain Technologies Limited, UK — a 100% acquisition on a debt-free, cash-free, normalized-working-capital basis for total consideration of USD 250 million (1.5x CY24 gross revenue), plus performance/time-linked deferred payouts in cash and stock over three years funded from Sojern cash flow. Sojern is described as a globally leading AI-powered marketing platform for travel and hospitality serving over 13,000 customers across hotels, destinations, attractions and travel brands, and its addition completed RateGain's Revenue Operating System by adding demand generation, travel intent intelligence and guest engagement to the existing pricing intelligence, revenue optimization, distribution and commercial data stack. It follows a track record of four earlier acquisitions — DHISCO (2018, integrated with RezGain's Channel Manager), BCV (2019, entry into MarTech), MyHotelShop (2021, metasearch/digital marketing) and Adara (2023, travel intent data and pricing intelligence) — and management states RateGain intends to continue pursuing inorganic growth targeting complementary products and technologies in a fragmented travel-technology landscape. The second expansion axis is go-to-market: approximately USD 5-6 million was deployed in FY 2025-26 towards building sales, customer success and account management teams, supported by investments in revenue operations and GTM enablement tools, with a major focus on scaling presence in high-growth markets, particularly APAC and the Middle East, where the GTM organization expanded substantially. During the year the Company also consolidated the platforms, brands, product teams and commercial organizations of Adara and Sojern into a unified MarTech business under the Sojern brand. Product-side expansion includes advancing the capabilities of AirGain, its specialist airline pricing intelligence tool, and extending solutions into adjacent travel verticals, new and underserved customer segments and new geographies through strategic partnerships with leading travel and hospitality brands.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global travel demand has remained resilient despite geopolitical tensions and lingering inflation, driven by consumers' increasing preference for premium, personalized and experience-led travel across major markets such as North America, Asia Pacific and the Middle East.
- Global international tourist arrivals reached 1.5 billion in 2025, growing 4% year-on-year, with momentum shifting eastward — Africa and Asia-Pacific led regional growth at 8% and 6% respectively.
- 74% of global travelers rank travel as their top discretionary spending priority, outpacing dining, fashion, electronics and wellness; the average global traveler expects to spend 9% more on trips in 2026 than in 2025, and over 91% of Indian travelers plan to increase travel budgets in 2026 (Chinese 65%, UK 61%).
- Skift Research projects approximately 5% top-line expansion for global travel in 2026, roughly 1.5x expected GDP growth; hotel sector growth is estimated at 4.9% in 2026 (down from 5.7% in 2025) with global hotel room revenues at ~USD 1,071 billion, airline revenue at USD 949 billion (up 5%), and OTA gross bookings at ~USD 912 billion growing ~6%.
- AI is reshaping how travelers discover, plan and book — search is becoming recommendation-led and AI is beginning to mediate decisions before brands enter the picture, shifting advantage toward platforms that control the customer journey and deliver personalized recommendations; more than half of consumers are likely or very likely to switch from their usual travel brand if an AI recommendation suggests a better alternative.
- The Middle East, South Asia and Southeast Asia are emerging as the new engines of global travel demand, redefining connectivity, infrastructure investment and hospitality standards — the UAE is investing over USD 35 billion in aviation infrastructure, Saudi Arabia more than USD 50 billion and India over USD 11 billion in airport infrastructure.
- A 'K-shaped' travel economy is forming: tariffs and inflation suppress purchasing power for middle-market travelers so luxury segments thrive while budget-conscious travelers make compromises (cheaper flights, shorter trips, less expensive destinations) rather than cancelling travel.
- Headwinds flagged: policy uncertainty, a softening job market, lingering effects of tariffs, shifting global alliances and unpredictable border policies; inbound travel to the U.S. has trended down since February 2025, with international arrivals estimated down 6% year-on-year in 2025.
- Global economic growth is at 3.4% in 2025, easing to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 (IMF World Economic Outlook, April 2026), weighed down by geopolitical tensions, trade fragmentation and softer global demand.
- Product-level performance levers management cites: AI-optimized audiences delivering 3-10x better campaign performance, an AI-native social platform automating 70% of tasks, a conversational revenue platform enabling up to 600% direct-bookings uplift, intelligent ARI logic optimizing ARI traffic by 30-40%, a 24x7 voice agent delivering up to 5x increase in direct bookings / 3x higher guest engagement / 40% revenue increase while addressing labor shortages in Europe and US markets, and an embedded payments layer that increased checkout conversions in India by 15% with a leading global OTA.
- Business-model resilience metrics cited for FY 2025-26: 94.9% gross revenue retention, 99.6% net revenue retention, 13,410 total customers, LTV to CAC of 12.8x (13.6x in FY 2024-25) and voluntary employee attrition of 14.7%.
- New contract wins of Rs 3,220 million in FY 2025-26, up 26%.
- Total pipeline of Rs 6,590 million, up 28%.
- The FIFA World Cup 2026 Market Pulse dashboard, built on Sojern's travel intent data and tracking booking signals across all 16 host cities in the US, Canada and Mexico, drew 200+ subscribers and converted interest into pipeline across Sojern, Navigator and Rev-AI.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

North America remains the Company's largest market while APAC is the fastest-growing region (team strength grown from 15 to 85 people during FY 2025-26) and Europe is the next investment priority following the Sojern footprint. Management explicitly notes the Middle East faced genuine headwinds during the year, so results remain exposed to region-specific demand shocks.
